zh.title: 歐洲飛安總署調降約旦領空警告風險
zh.summary: 約旦、黎巴嫩航警降級；貝魯特機場有條件恢復
body: 歐洲聯盟航空安全總署（European Union Aviation Safety Agency，EASA）於2026年8月31日調降對約旦及黎巴嫩的空域警告，同日約旦軍方表示，在黎明時分攔截了八枚飛進王國空域的飛彈。EASA修訂針對約旦的衝突區域資訊公報（Conflict Zone Information Bulletin，CZIB），取消建議營運業者全面避免進入安曼飛航情報區（FIR）的建議，並將涉入風險評估為中等而非高風險。
修訂後的公報要求營運業者考量潛在風險、維持最新的風險評估與應變計畫，並準備好在短期通知後遵循國家當局的指示。EASA將此變更歸因於2026年8月空域相對安靜，並指出約旦當局未發布與衝突相關的空域限制或航路關閉，營運業者應準備在活動恢復時進行戰術隔離。
同日，約旦武裝部隊官方發言人在國家新聞社Petra的聲明表示，防空系統攔截了於2026年8月31日黎明時侵入王國空域的八枚飛彈，並稱飛彈在被摧毀前未對公民或財產構成威脅。
EASA也修訂了黎巴嫩的公報，恢復貝魯特哈里里國際機場（BEY）的限制，允許在到達與離場均位於海上時進出貝魯特，且需有最新的風險評估與持續監控。黎巴嫩領空除該例外區域外，仍被評估為高風險，EASA指出2026年8月在黎巴嫩南部觀察到一再的停火遊約遭破壞。
另據國家新聞社WAM報導，阿拉伯聯合大公國國防部於2026年8月31日表示，其空軍攔截了一架在領海上空接近的大量無人機，並稱其來自伊朗。EASA曾在2026年7月14日建議航空業者避開巴林、科威特、卡達及阿拉伯聯合大公國的海灣空域。
兩份修訂後的公報效力至2026年9月30日，除非提早審查。CZIB屬建議性質，適用於受歐盟規則965/2012管制的營運商及擁有EASA授權的第三國營運商，而各國政府仍對其領空擁有控制權。

en.title: EASA lowers Jordan airspace warning; eight missiles intercepted in a single day
en.summary: EASA eased Jordan, Lebanon warnings; Beirut access restored with conditions; missiles intercepted
body: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) downgraded its airspace warnings for Jordan and Lebanon on August 31, 2026, the same day Jordan’s military said it intercepted eight missiles over the kingdom at dawn.

The agency revised its Conflict Zone Information Bulletin (CZIB) for Jordan, dropping the recommendation that operators avoid the Amman flight information region (FIR) altogether. The revised bulletin asks operators to take potential risks into account, maintain updated risk assessments and contingency plans, and remain prepared to follow instructions from state authorities at short notice. EASA assessed the risk to civil flights as medium rather than high and extended the bulletin’s validity to September 30, 2026.

The revision was attributed to a quiet August 2026, with no kinetic military activity observed after a sustained increase in July. Jordanian authorities have published no conflict-related airspace restrictions or route closures, so operators should be prepared for tactical deconfliction if activity resumes.

The official spokesman for the Jordanian Armed Forces said through the state news agency Petra that air defense systems intercepted eight missiles that penetrated the kingdom's airspace at dawn on August 31, 2026, destroying them before they posed a threat to citizens or property.

EASA also restored a limited exception for Beirut Rafic Hariri International Airport (BEY), allowing flights to and from Beirut when the approach and departure are over the hot seat, subject to continuous risk monitoring. Lebanese airspace remains high risk outside that carve-out, with recurrent ceasefire violations observed in August 2026, primarily in southern Lebanon.

Separately, the UAE Ministry of Defense said on August 31, 2026, that the UAE Air Force engaged a drone detected over territorial waters as it approached from Iran, in a statement carried by the WAM. EASA had advised airlines to avoid Gulf airspace covering Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE on July 14, 2026.
